The member figures in this card are wrong, and the correction makes option B slightly less bad rather than better.** The reviewer counted `NamedListView`'s top-level members with the pin's own regex, at PR #7922's head and at its merge-base: **47**, not "about 52" — so **40** unread, not ~45 (the 59 that a looser count produces includes nested lines). Read every "~52 / ~45" above as **47 / 40**. The shape of the argument is unchanged: 7 read, 40 unread.

**2. ⚠️ Option C is not simply "the ruled route applied to this key."** The ruling that produced PR #7922 says the spec-modelled keys are mirrored **by reference to the spec slot**. `listViews` is one of those four. Option C — mirror the seven members the renderer reads and retire the rest — is a **local** shape, so choosing it means deciding that for this one key the local vocabulary is the contract and the spec slot is not, which is a different decision from the one already made for `navigation` / `searchableFields` / `filterableFields`. That is not an argument against C; it is the thing to decide knowingly rather than by momentum.

**3. ⚠️ Whichever face is chosen breaks a live writer.** They are not symmetric costs on paper only:
- choosing the **spec** face (A) breaks the documentation — `packages/plugin-view/README.md:154` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-view.mdx:72` teach the label-only view, `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md:863-864` teaches the tuple filter and `default` — and it does **not** break app-shell's `ViewPreview.tsx`, which already writes the spec shape;
- choosing the **local** face (B or C) keeps the docs green and breaks **`ViewPreview.tsx` (~`:111-115`)**, which spreads a spec-shaped view body into `listViews` today.

So "no option is free" is not a rhetorical hedge here — each names a specific site that has to change with it. Option D (stay ledgered) remains the zero-cost interim and is what `main` carries after PR #7922 lands.

## The census this card was waiting on is done — and it says the 41 unread members are **not one population**

`domain:spec` @ objectui PM seat, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`. Input: **PR #8933** (objectui#7924), measured on `3b5053d45`. ⛔ Recording and structuring the ruling request only — **not proposing that any particular route be taken**, and ⛔ nothing here changes this card's `pm:blocked` state on its own.

### What was measured, and how

`NamedListView` is walked with the **TypeScript parser** (`ts.createSourceFile`, the interface's own `PropertySignature` members) — ⛔ not a regex, ⛔ not a brace-depth count. The read set is derived by walking **every route** from `schema.listViews` to a named view, and every occurrence of that record is **classified**, so a new route lands as `UNCLASSIFIED` and fails rather than silently shrinking the reading.

```
declared members                 47      (plain interface: no heritage clause,
                                          no index signature, no computed member —
                                          so its property signatures ARE the population)
required members                  1      `label`
read off a named view             7 names — 6 declared + `data`, which is declared NOWHERE
declared and unread              41      = 47 − 6, ⛔ not 47 − 7
```

Controls on the same instruments: firing `columns` (declared **and** read); negative twin `rowHeight` (declared, **not** read off a named view — it is read off `activeView`, which is the distinction the whole finding turns on); absent `stickyHeader` (in neither set). Each of the 47 is pinned **by name** on its side, so a member moving fails **in either direction**.

⚠️ **Three of objectui#7924's own figures did not survive re-derivation** and are corrected on that card: "about 52" was a hand figure sitting between two regex instruments and equal to neither (strict, indent-anchored: **47** = the parser; loose: **59**, because it also counts nested object-literal lines); "~45" wrongly subtracted `data`, which is read but not declared; and "exactly seven **members**" should be seven *names*, six of them members.

⚠️ **And the instrument this card has been quoting was blind.** The `currentNamedViewConfig?.KEY` regex cannot see `{view.label || key}` on the tab strip, reached through `Object.entries(schema.listViews).map(([key, view]) => …)`. `label` is read at **two** sites, not one. Repaired inside PR #8933.

### ⭐ The ruling, split four ways — because one question about 41 keys is the wrong question

The routes this card names — `?: never` tombstones (narrowing a published accept set) versus making the delegation read the members from the named view (capability growth) — do **not** price the same for all 41. The census separates them:

| group | n | what it is | why the two routes price differently here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | **34** | a host-side twin the renderer **honours off `activeView`** — `rowHeight`, `navigation`, `selection`, `pagination`, `searchableFields`, … | ⛔ The behaviour **exists**; only the *source* is wrong. A tombstone tells an author the key is dead while the feature is live on the other source. This is the genuinely hard half. |
| **B** | **4** | reached **only** through the `normalizeListViewSchema(activeView)` fold — `showHideFields`, `showGroup`, `showColor`, `showDensity` | ⚠️ **A named-property probe reports these dead. They are not.** Consumed by a whole-object fold, never by a named read. Recorded because that artifact would otherwise have walked straight into this ruling as four extra dead keys. |
| **C** | **3** | **no reader on any path** — `description`, `exportOptions`, `bulkActionDefs`. The last two do not appear in the renderer **at all**, pinned with a firing control | The only group where "declared, unenforced, unread" has nothing to weigh against it. |
| **D** | **1** | **`data`** — read through an `as any` cast, declared nowhere | This card requires it declared or the cast removed, and names objectui#7924 as its home. The census answers: **still neither.** |

⇒ **C and D are the cheap, unambiguous halves** — C is a genuine tombstone candidate, D is a two-line decision. **A and B are the part that is really "capability growth vs. narrow a published accept set"**, because for those the behaviour exists and only the source is wrong. `label` is the sole required member and it **is** read, so no route disturbs it.

### ⛔ What is NOT claimed here

⛔ No disposition is chosen, for any group. ⛔ No declaration face has moved: `objectql.ts`, every `*.zod.ts` and every renderer read set are untouched by PR #8933, which is `Clause-②: no` and test-only. The census is the input; the ruling is the maintainer's.
